children: Retail investors increased their options activity in cybersecurity stocks during the recent rally but remained net sellers of some underlying shares, suggesting there could be further room for cash buying if the sector's gains continue, according to Vanda Analytics.

Institutional positioning also appeared relatively light ahead of the move. Vanda's institutional call-put ratio score for its cybersecurity basket stood at -0.27 as of Sept. 14, below its median since 2017 and well below the +0.84 recorded in January. Institutional call demand had also been fading since early summer, the firm said.
The positioning came ahead of the Global X Cybersecurity ETF
recording its biggest one-day gain on record, according to Vanda.
Retail participation, meanwhile, was concentrated in options rather than the underlying stocks. Retail out-of-the-money call turnover across CrowdStrike
jumped into the 98th percentile of its history over the past five sessions, Vanda said.
But cash flows pointed in the opposite direction. Retail investors were net sellers of $6.4M of Palo Alto Networks and $3.5M of Zscaler in the previous session, according to Vanda.

The data showed that retail investors participated in the cybersecurity rally mainly through short-dated options rather than by rebuilding outright positions in the underlying stocks, said Viraj Patel, chief innovation officer and global market strategist at Vanda Analytics.
That leaves potential room for retail cash buying to increase if the cybersecurity rally extends, Patel said.

title: Retail traders chased cyber options but skipped the stocks
